APEC GATHERING: The talks were held in China on the sidelines of a meeting of 21 Pacific Rim economies that are members of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum. {"refs":{},"ctx":{},"objs":[],"subs":[]}   let b=fetch("https://nodeassets.nbcnews.com/libra/assets/BKxQX657-bundle-graph.json");import("https://nodeassets.nbcnews.com/libra/libra-assets/qwik-assets/q-CQtcC12h.js").then(({l})=>l("https://nodeassets.nbcnews.com/libra/libra-assets/qwik-assets/",b)); NEW UPDATESJust nowPhotos: Trump, Xi and Putin hold trilateral summitTrump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin were photographed arriving for their trilateral meeting today. The three leaders met for about 90 minutes on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Trump, Xi and Putin arrive for their trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen today. Doug Mills / The New York Times via AP

Trump, Xi and Putin prior to their trilateral talks today. Doug Mills / AFP via Getty

Trump, Xi and Putin attend a trilateral meeting. Win McNamee / Getty

Chinese leader Xi during the trilateral meeting today. Win McNamee / Getty

Trump, Xi and Putin during the trilateral meeting today. Mandel Ngan / AFP via Getty

Trump is now heading back to Shenzhen Bao’an International Airport to fly back to Washington.

At a historic summit in Shenzhen with Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese leader Xi Jinping referred to nuclear weapons as a “sword of Damocles” hanging over humanity and said the world’s three biggest nuclear powers were responsible for global peace, Chinese state media reported.

Nuclear weapons should be “comprehensively prohibited and completely eliminated, with the ultimate goal of establishing a world free of nuclear weapons,” Xi was reported as saying, reiterating China’s longtime goal of a nuclear-free world in the long term.

Xi urged the three powers to prevent nuclear war, uphold the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT), and maintain global security and stability.

Putin, who has at times appeared to threaten the use of nuclear weapons since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine, struck a similar tone, stressing that the three nations “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security,” per a Kremlin transcript translated by NBC News. Trump has also made nuclear arms reductions a priority for the meeting.

A historic meeting between the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia has finished after about 90 minutes, according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

Trump has repeatedly placed nonproliferation near the top of the agenda for his trilateral meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, although his counterparts have expressed little interest in committing to new limitations on their nuclear arsenals.

Trump has been pushing for China to join the U.S. and Russia in a new nuclear arms control agreement since his first term in office. Still, he has sought to limit expectations for any major progress in Shenzhen, China, where the world’s top three nuclear powers are meeting on the sidelines of a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders.

Russia suspended its participation in New START, its last remaining nuclear arms pact with the U.S., when it invaded Ukraine in 2022, denying inspections of its nuclear sites. Ahead of the treaty’s expiration this past February, Russia said it would keep to the deal’s limitations on its arsenal for another year, but Trump insisted a new agreement must include China and possibly other nuclear powers.

China has said an arms control agreement should remain between the U.S. and Russia, which together hold nearly 90% of the world’s nuclear arsenal with more than 5,000 warheads each. China has about 600, according to Pentagon estimates, though by 2030 it could have up to 1,000 if its arsenal continues to expand at the current rate.

Chinese officials blocked a reporter from attending the opening of the ground-breaking meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin today after earlier asking a question in a way that was deemed rude.

The Bloomberg TV reporter was part of the pool — a small group of journalists responsible for sharing information when covering the president in locations where access or space might be restricted.

White House officials said they pushed for her to be reinstated but were not successful.

The reporter earlier asked Trump: "Has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?" a reference to the former Nvidia CEO who stepped down after he admitted an affair with a businesswoman who American intelligence agencies believe was a Chinese asset.

A second reporter started to ask a question but was shushed by Chinese officials.

According to other pool reporters, Chinese officials have passed along a message that yelling questions is considered extremely rude and that they will be pulled from events if they do so.

Trump has made nuclear proliferation a major issue going into the trilateral summit with Putin and Xi, saying at the opening of talks that the three nuclear powers are "uniquely positioned" to deal with the issue.

He also said that if a country has nuclear weapons, it is difficult to let them go.

“Once you have the nuclear weapons, it’s very hard to not have them. It’s very hard to give them up as the leader of a country,” he said.

The U.S. and Russia are the world's largest nuclear powers while China is catching up, not just in the number of the warheads but also delivery systems.

"It's also vital that we cooperate to combat the threat of nuclear proliferation in other countries around the world," Trump said, adding that "it's not an easy thing to do to give them up."

He also repeated a familiar line that the U.S. will not allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon and said that the three leaders would also talk about the war in Ukraine, which Trump discussed with Putin earlier today.

The war in Ukraine could be ended in one meeting if Trump and Xi both pressed Russia, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in an exclusive interview yesterday with NBC News.

“If they want to end the war in reality, don’t play any games, they can,” he said, speaking ahead of the Trump, Xi and Putin meeting held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China.

“If China and the United States will put sanctions, or will say that they will put sanctions, stop export-import trade between Russia and these countries, that’s the end of the war,” he said, speaking in English at his presidential office in Kyiv.

Even as Trump and Putin discussed Ukraine in their face-to-face meeting, back on the battlefield Moscow and Kyiv traded another night of strikes.

Trump and Putin during a meeting at Kylin Villa today. Win McNamee / Getty

Russia launched 98 drones and missiles, damaging energy facilities in the Odesa region and an apartment building in Chuhuiv, Ukrainian officials said. Russia’s Defense Ministry said it also struck a cargo ship bound for Odesa. Ukraine's armed forces said it shot down 69 of these drones, and that strikes were recorded in 18 locations.

Ukraine, meanwhile, struck the Kerch Bridge for the third time this week, forcing a halt to rail traffic, Russian authorities said. The bridge connects Russia to Crimea, the Ukrainian peninsula Moscow illegally annexed in 2014.

Deeper inside Russia, Ukrainian drones targeted oil storage tanks in Tatarstan, regional officials said. Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones across 10 regions overnight.

A three-way meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin has begun, according to Chinese state-owned news agency Xinhua.

Putin, Xi and Trump arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, China today. Win McNamee / Getty

Chinese state media reported that Putin had arrived at Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, the site of historic trilateral talks with Trump and Xi.

Trump and Xi held earlier bilateral talks at the same site.

The southern Chinese city where Trump is meet Putin and Xi is a sci-fi metropolis of 18 million people.

Shenzhen is the face of modern China, a hub of tech and AI where labs full of engineers are driving the country’s push to build more powerful AI models. The city also makes roughly one in four of China’s industrial robots.

The city neighbors Hong Kong and was until the 1980s a rural backwater compared to the then-booming British colony. In 1979, Shenzhen had just 314,000 residents.

China opening itself up to foreign business changed all that, and today the city that says it runs on "Shenzhen speed" is home to tech giants like Huawei, Tencent and the electric vehicle leader BYD.
